Let me analyze the code against the spec.

The spec: `slugify(title)` turns a title into a URL slug: lowercase ASCII letters and digits only, words joined by single HYPHENS, no leading or trailing hyphen. Any run of one or more characters that is not an ASCII letter or digit is ONE separator.

The current implementation:
```elixir
title
|> String.downcase()
|> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
```

This replaces each non-alphanumeric char with a hyphen individually, so multiple separators produce multiple hyphens. Also doesn't strip leading/trailing hyphens.

Examples:
- "Hello, World!" => "hello-world": with current impl: "hello--world-" (comma -> -, space -> -, ! -> -, plus trailing). Wait "Hello, World!" = H-e-l-l-o-,-space-W... "hello," -> "hello-", then " " -> "-", so "hello--world" then "!" -> "-": "hello--world-". Wrong.
- "  A--B  " => "a-b": current "  a--b  " -> "--a--b--" wrong.

So the fix: use regex to collapse runs `[^a-z0-9]+` -> "-", then trim leading/trailing hyphens. Also need to handle the empty case: "" => "".

Let me write:
```elixir
def slugify(title) when is_binary(title) do
  title
  |> String.downcase()
  |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, "-")
  |> String.trim("-")
end
```

Check "" => "" : downcase "" -> "", replace -> "", trim "-" -> "". Good.

Check "  A--B  " => downcase "  a--b  " -> replace `[^a-z0-9]+`: the "  " (two spaces) is one run -> "-", "a", "--" -> "-", "b", "  " -> "-" => "-a-b-". trim("-") -> "a-b". 

Check "Hello, World!" => "hello" then ", " is a run (comma + space) -> "-", "world", "!" -> "-" => "hello-world-". trim -> "hello-world". 

Check "Elixir 1.19" => "elixir" " " -> "-", "1", "." -> "-", "19" => "elixir-1-19". Good.

Edge: what about a title that's all separators, e.g. "---" => replace -> "-", trim -> "". Good, no leading/trailing hyphen.

Also need to be careful: `String.trim("-")` trims all leading/trailing "-". Since we collapsed runs, there's at most one leading and one trailing. Good.
